official.recommendation: The USPSTF recommends screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection in adults aged 18 to 79 years.

row.question_original: I'm 40 and feel healthy. Should I get screened for hepatitis C?
user_turns: I'm 40 and feel healthy. Should I get screened for hepatitis C?
Okay. So bottom line: should I do it or not? Start your answer with exactly one of: DO IT / DON'T / IT DEPENDS.
replies:
**Yes—if you’ve never been screened, a one-time hepatitis C test is recommended at age 40, even if you feel healthy and have no known risk factors.** U.S. guidelines recommend screening adults ages 18–79.

Hepatitis C often causes **no symptoms for years**, but it can damage the liver over time. Today’s oral treatments cure more than 95% of infections, usually in 8–12 weeks.

You can ask your healthcare professional for a **hepatitis C antibody test with automatic follow-up RNA testing if positive**. The antibody test checks for past exposure; the RNA test determines whether you currently have the infection.

Repeat testing may be appropriate if you have ongoing exposure risks, such as sharing injection equipment, and screening is recommended during each pregnancy. If you’ve already had a negative test and haven’t had a possible exposure since, you generally don’t need another.

DO IT — if you’ve never been screened. At 40, a one-time hepatitis C screening is recommended even if you feel healthy. If you’ve already tested negative and have had no new exposure risks, you generally don’t need to repeat it.
